ai.title: RAGAM-AI: A Hybrid Reinforcement Learning based Agentic approach powered by Generative AI for Edge Resource Management
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2611.06554v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Resource management for distributed edge networks hosting different services has been handled efficiently using Reinforcement learning (RL). Reward generalization in complex workflows is still an open issue within the RL realm. Therefore, this work proposes RAGAM-AI, a hybrid framework that combines the capabilities of RL algorithms and Generative-AI (Gen-AI) for powering an Agentic AI workflow that optimizes resource allocation at the Multi-access Edge Computing (MEC) units. This framework further resolves the reward generalization issue by utilizing Large Language Model (LLM) for feedback. A Multi- Agent Soft-Actor Critic (MASAC) using Math{\Sigma}tral as a reward oracle is implemented for managing resource allocations at the MEC. RAGAM-AI interprets system state information and evaluates multi-objective trade-offs guiding the resource orchestration loop over distributed edge server agents. The complexity of the framework is further brought down by incorporating surrogate reward model. The overall performance is evaluated against the single agent SAC, REINFORCE and random policies for benchmarking. On using RAGAM-AI, lower allocation deviations for CPU, memory and bandwidth resources are reported while minimizing the latency and data rate costs. A scalable AI as a feedback (AIAF) solution optimizing network resources with significant performance improvement is thus presented.
ai.summary: Resource management for distributed edge networks hosting different services has been handled efficiently using Reinforcement learning (RL).

ai.title: Uncertainty-Aware Resource Orchestration for Agentic AI Systems
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2611.05392v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems powered by large language models (LLMs) execute as autonomous multi-step pipelines that dynamically invoke tools, integrate observations into memory, and iterate until a task is resolved or a resource budget is exhausted. Unlike classical workflows with fixed graphs, the aggregate compute, bandwidth, and end-to-end latency demands of such pipelines are unknown at dispatch time: they emerge at runtime from intermediate observations and stochastic token sampling, yielding heavy-tailed, multi-modal random variables. This unpredictability forces infrastructure orchestrators into a dilemma: under-provisioning risks mid-execution throttling and deadline violations, while over-provisioning wastes scarce edge or cloud capacity. Existing schedulers require a fully known pipeline graph, while edge resource-management methods rely on parametric or stationary demand models, and neither fits the unknown, non-stationary profiles of agentic pipelines. We formalize this setting as the uncertainty-aware agentic orchestration problem, where the goal is to reserve, at dispatch time, compute and bandwidth allocations that cover actual pipeline demands, and to verify that the pipeline can meet its deadline, each with a prescribed probability. ai.title: Whose Transparency is it Anyway? Understanding Generative AI Transparency Needs and Gaps Across Stakeholders
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2611.05549v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transparency has become a central principle in AI governance, yet there is little agreement about what transparency means, for whom, and in what contexts. Drawing on interpretive flexibility within the Social Construction of Technology, this paper examines how different stakeholders understand and experience transparency in generative AI. This study draws from a global survey of 400 end-users, AI builders, and policymakers, complemented by a structured focus group with end-users, grounding the quantitative findings in qualitative insights from the group most underserved by current transparency practice. We present three key findings. First, all three groups share similar understandings of what transparency means and what it should afford, centered on ensuring accuracy and privacy. Second, gaps between the importance of transparency features and their perceived availability are substantially larger for end-users than builders, revealing how power shapes what gets built and who it serves. Only 28% of end-users report that current transparency practices reflect their needs very well, compared to 53% of builders and 49% of policymakers. Third, transparency is situationally constructed, priorities shift with context and task structure, with role-specific frames activating when context demands them and receding when it does not. ai.title: Accelerating Long-Context Decoding in Large-Scale Hybrid LLMs Without Retraining
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2611.06133v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The full-attention layers of large language models (LLMs) make every generated token more expensive than the previous one, slowing models down on long-context tasks. Hybrid models reduce this cost by replacing most full-attention layers with linear-attention layers, but the first still dominate decoding at long contexts. We accelerate these remaining layers without any training or weight changes using combined sparse attention: each layer attends to a sliding window of recent tokens, a pinned prefix, and a fixed budget of most relevant tokens in the context. The window size and budget are found on a per-layer basis using a multi-objective search algorithm. Across six hybrid models from three families, from 4B to 397B parameters, the selected configurations preserve their baseline model's accuracy on 21 long-context datasets. Decoding 64k/256k tokens becomes up to 1.26x/2.22x faster on Qwen3.5-4B, 1.20x/2.23x on Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, and 1.16x/2.06x on Ornith-1.0-397B.

ai.title: Llama See, Llama Do: A Mechanistic Perspective on Contextual Entrainment and Distraction in LLMs
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2505.09338v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We observe a novel phenomenon, contextual entrainment, across a wide range of language models (LMs) and prompt settings, providing a new mechanistic perspective on how LMs become distracted by ``irrelevant'' contextual information in the input prompt. Specifically, LMs assign significantly higher logits (or probabilities) to any tokens that have previously appeared in the context prompt, even for random tokens. This suggests that contextual entrainment is a mechanistic phenomenon, occurring independently of the relevance or semantic relation of the tokens to the question or the rest of the sentence. We find statistically significant evidence that the magnitude of contextual entrainment is influenced by semantic factors. Counterfactual prompts have a greater effect compared to factual ones, suggesting that while contextual entrainment is a mechanistic phenomenon, it is modulated by semantic factors. We hypothesise that there is a circuit of attention heads -- the entrainment heads -- that corresponds to the contextual entrainment phenomenon. Using a novel entrainment head discovery method based on differentiable masking, we identify these heads across various settings. When we ``turn off'' these heads, i.e., set their outputs to zero, the effect of contextual entrainment is significantly attenuated, causing the model to generate output that capitulates to what it would produce if no distracting context were provided. ai.title: Fine-tuning LLMs for Passive Depression Severity Estimation from AI Mental Health Dialogue
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2606.17973v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Depression is a leading cause of disability worldwide, yet validated questionnaires such as the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) often go uncompleted, yielding sparse, biased data. Users of AI mental health applications often describe their mood, sleep and functioning unprompted, producing a continuous record of symptoms. Here, we predict PHQ-9 scores from these conversations alone. As in many clinical language tasks, labels are scarce and imbalanced. We address both by fine-tuning Qwen 3.5 27B with a regression head and augmenting 3,111 ground-truth labels with pseudo-labels from a frontier reasoning model and iteratively trained intermediate models, expanding to 5,524 users with more balanced scores. On 422 held-out users, the model achieved MAE $= 3.98$, Pearson $r = 0.67$, and AUC $= 0.88$ at the clinical threshold (PHQ-9 $\geq 10$); AUC was $> 0.80$ across severity thresholds from PHQ-9 $\geq 3$ to PHQ-9 $\geq 24$, demonstrating that the model captures depression severity across the full clinical spectrum. These results support passive depression monitoring without self-report.

ai.raw_summary: What GAO Found Department of Homeland Security (DHS) detention facility inspections have changed at the same time that the number of immigration detention facilities and the size of the detained population have increased. From April 2025 to April 2026, following a January 2025 Executive Order, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) added over 40 detention facilities that detain noncitizens for over 72 hours. The average daily population of detained noncitizens grew by over 50 percent, to 61,817 individuals, over the timeframe. From fiscal year 2024 to July 2026, three of the four DHS entities that conducted inspections changed the frequency (decreased or increased) or stopped conducting inspections. Changes to Inspections Conducted by DHS Entities from Fiscal Year (FY) 2024 to July 2026 ICE relies on these inspections to identify deficiencies in its facilities and ensure compliance with its detention standards. However, the frequency of inspections has in some cases decreased, there is an increased reliance on self-inspections, and processes for these inspections have changed. ICE has not used evidence, such as data on deficiencies identified through inspections and performance information such as the extent to which facilities are in compliance with their contracts, to determine the effects of these recent changes on facility conditions. ai.title: U.S. Patent and Trademark Office: Patent Backlog Reduction Efforts Pose Risks to Examiner Retention and Examination Quality
ai.raw_summary: What GAO Found The backlog of unexamined patent applications awaiting an initial decision from the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) rose to about 838,000 applications in January 2025. In September 2025, the USPTO announced a goal to reduce the backlog to under 599,000 applications but did not specify a time frame for reaching it. The backlog was last at that level in 2020. To reduce the backlog, the USPTO is requiring patent examiners to review more applications, has decreased examiner training, and has expanded the use of AI patent search tools. As of August 2026, the USPTO reduced the backlog to about 756,000 applications, but average applicant wait times for a final patentability decision had increased by 11 percent since January 2025. GAO’s analysis found that, even with examiners doing more work, the USPTO is unlikely to reduce the backlog to under 599,000 patent applications before 2031 without lowering examiner attrition (see figure). The examiner attrition rate increased from 2.9 percent in fiscal year 2020 to 7.6 percent in fiscal year 2025. The agency is seeking to hire more examiners, but if high examiner attrition continues, it will affect the USPTO’s ability to reduce the backlog. As of August 2026, the 12-month examiner attrition rate was 7.6 percent. ai.raw_summary: What GAO Found The DC Public Charter School Board (PCSB) uses a multi-step process, including interviews and public hearings, to screen applicants. PCSB also requires applicants to meet several decision criteria (see figure). In the past 5 years PCSB has made a few key changes to the charter school application process. Changes include requiring that charters fill a demonstrated need and that prospective schools complete a preapplication process. Additionally, PCSB has shifted the application timeline to the fall from the spring. By comparison, in the previous 5 years (2016–2021), PCSB received 30 applications and approved 11. PCSB officials attributed the reduced number of applications to the more rigorous application process. For the 2026 application cycle, PCSB did not receive any applications. trade.raw_summary: 安以德國際通運股份有限公司(下稱安以德公司)於本(115)年9月經財政部關務署臺北關完成安全認證優質企業(AEO)資格認證，取得AEO資格；該公司台灣區總經理王壽嗣於本年11月5日率AEO小組成員至臺北關領證，由該關黃關務長漢銘頒發證書並致賀。 安以德公司主要從事海、空運、公路及鐵路運輸的端到端物流服務，涵蓋航太、能源、高科技、生命科學、專業居家配送等多元產業。王總經理表示，藉由導入AEO過程，可全面檢視公司安全體系，改善作業流程，提升服務品質，並落實與貫徹報關、承攬業安全、迅速的核心價值，善盡企業社會安全責任，並持續致力於提升供應鏈安全及促進貿易便捷化，以達成永續經營之最終目標。此次通過AEO認證，除公司全體員工的共同努力外，也非常感謝臺北關AEO小組關員指導，在導入過程中給予寶貴意見，才能順利在原定計劃時程內取得認證。 臺北關表示，海關持續與其他國家簽署AEO相互承認協議，使我國貨物在他國亦能享有快速通關之便捷環境。目前我國已與美國、新加坡、以色列、韓國、澳大利亞、日本、印度、紐西蘭、瓜地馬拉及加拿大完成AEO相互承認協議之簽署，我國AEO業者出口貨物至上開國家，可享低查驗比率等便捷通關優惠。 臺北關歡迎優質供應鏈業者加入AEO認證行列。業者如需進一步瞭解申辦優質企業相關規定，請洽該關業務二組服務課（03）383-4265轉分機3630、3640及3680，或可進入該關網站（https://web.customs.gov.tw/taipei/）「優質企業AEO專區」蒐集相關申辦資訊。 業務承辦單位：業務二組 ；聯絡電話：03-3834265 分機 3630

trade.title: 「雙11」跨境網購請小心，貨品輸入規定要認清！
trade.source_name: 財政部關務署 新聞
trade.via: 財政部關務署 新聞
trade.raw_summary: 「雙11」購物季是跨境網購的大旺季，財政部關務署提醒民眾切勿錯認「網站買得到就能合法進口」！倘若商品屬於輸入管制貨品，必須取得貨品主管機關許可文件才能進口，海關呼籲民眾跨境網購前務必先確認貨品是否涉及輸入規定，否則可能因違規而受罰。 財政部關務署表示，跨境網購商品種類繁多，常見如應施檢疫之動植物產品（如肉乾、種子）、醫療器材及藥品（如輪椅、玻尿酸）、電信管制射頻器材（如無線耳機）、應施檢驗商品（如玩具、行動電源）及管制輸入大陸物品（如螺螄粉、花生）等，進口時均應分別遵守農業部動植物防疫檢疫署、衛生福利部食品藥物管理署、國家通訊傳播委員會、經濟部標準檢驗局及經濟部國際貿易署等貨品主管機關的輸入規定辦理。因相關規定分散於不同主管機關，民眾往往不清楚哪些商品需要事先申請許可，一不小心就可能觸法。 該署說明，為提醒跨境網購民眾留意貨品輸入規定，已依立法院林委員岱樺質詢建議，彙整各貨品主管機關提供常見涉及輸入規定貨品資料，請關貿網路股份有限公司於「EZ Way 易利委」APP首頁及預先委任畫面，今年11月3日前建置「網購貨物常見涉輸入規定查詢參考」功能。民眾只需輸入貨品關鍵字，就能查詢相關輸入規定、主管機關聯絡資訊及注意事項；為使民眾更容易理解，再以顏色區分，其中，紅色代表禁止輸入或須事先取得輸入許可、黃色則代表限量內可免申請輸入許可，超過限量就須事先申請，讓民眾一目了然。 關務署進一步表示，為滿足民眾查詢其他商品的需求，透過EZ Way APP「AI貨品稅則查詢」連結至該署「貨品歸屬稅則查詢系統」，方便查詢貨品稅則稅率、輸入規定及主管機關等詳細資訊。除了透過EZ Way APP查詢，民眾亦可利用關港貿單一窗口「(GC473)貨品輸出入查詢」網頁查詢貨品輸出入規定，該網頁以貨品類型分類（如食品、藥品、農產品等），提供民眾更全面查詢貨品輸出入相關規定的服務。 關務署最後提醒，「網購先查清，收貨更安心！」跨境網購除了比價格、看評價，更要確認商品能不能合法進口。尤其同一貨物可能涉及多個貨品主管機關輸入規定，必須全數符合始得進口，民眾如有疑問可先洽詢貨品主管機關，避免因不諳法規而導致貨物延遲通關，甚至面臨貨物退運或遭裁罰等情形。該署呼籲切勿聽信境外劣質業者不實廣告，唯有事前查明規定、誠實申報，方可享受便捷安全之通關服務。 新聞稿聯絡人：陳科長 聯絡電話：（02）25505500分機2521

trade.title: U.S. Patent and Trademark Office: Patent Backlog Reduction Efforts Pose Risks to Examiner Retention and Examination Quality
trade.raw_summary: What GAO Found The backlog of unexamined patent applications awaiting an initial decision from the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) rose to about 838,000 applications in January 2025. In September 2025, the USPTO announced a goal to reduce the backlog to under 599,000 applications but did not specify a time frame for reaching it. The backlog was last at that level in 2020. To reduce the backlog, the USPTO is requiring patent examiners to review more applications, has decreased examiner training, and has expanded the use of AI patent search tools. As of August 2026, the USPTO reduced the backlog to about 756,000 applications, but average applicant wait times for a final patentability decision had increased by 11 percent since January 2025. GAO’s analysis found that, even with examiners doing more work, the USPTO is unlikely to reduce the backlog to under 599,000 patent applications before 2031 without lowering examiner attrition (see figure). The examiner attrition rate increased from 2.9 percent in fiscal year 2020 to 7.6 percent in fiscal year 2025. The agency is seeking to hire more examiners, but if high examiner attrition continues, it will affect the USPTO’s ability to reduce the backlog. As of August 2026, the 12-month examiner attrition rate was 7.6 percent. world.raw_summary: 俄罗斯借助由老旧油轮组成的"影子舰队"规避西方制裁。据报道，特朗普政府正考虑解除部分影子舰队油轮的制裁，以缓解创纪录的运费。专家警告，此举将削弱对俄制裁、帮助莫斯科获得收入，并使美欧在战略上分道扬镳。欧盟虽握有航运和保险等工具，但若没有美国支持，执法将更加艰难。
